headline: Nine Elite Banks Helped Move $2.25 Billion in Dirty Cash; Singapore Sends a $21.5 Million Bill
deck: Singapore fined Credit Suisse, UOB, UBS, Citi, Julius Baer, LGT and three peers S$27.45 million — 0.915% of the Fujian laundering haul.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Nine financial institutions fined S$27.45M (~$21.5M) combined — exactly 0.915% of S$3.0B laundered, earning formal FATF criticism.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Laundering $1,800 in illicit cash and receiving a 0.915% civil bill
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: At Singapore’s institutional bank rate, the penalty would be $16.47 and zero jail time

sources.title: MAS Takes Regulatory Actions Against 9 Financial Institutions for AML-Related Breaches (S$27.45 Million)
FATF/APG Mutual Evaluation Report of Singapore (Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Measures)

interactive_art_spec.caption: Marina Bay in Singapore. Nine banks paid a combined S$27.45 million after S$3 billion in Fujian laundering funds moved through the city-state.
